blindSummary: This state/province combines high recorded lethality with an advanced legislature. It recorded the second-highest count among units in the 2021 national report of violent deaths of LGBTQ+ people (9, in a year led by another unit with 10), and has remained among the units with the highest counts in subsequent years. It was simultaneously the first state/province in the country to pass a comprehensive sexual-and-gender-diversity law - approved unanimously by all 32 deputies across the governing and opposition parties on 15 February 2024 and published 7 June 2024 - and it amended its penal code the same year to add sexual orientation and gender identity as protected characteristics. But an international human-rights group devoted a March 2024 documentary to discrimination against trans people in this state/province over identity documents, and a federal court had to order the unit's legislature in June 2024 to create a rights-respecting recognition procedure - the statute book moved faster than the administration that must apply it.

An international human-rights group's report (6 March 2024) on a neighbouring unit: no legal gender recognition procedure there exposes trans people to institutional mistreatment - the August 2023 killing of an activist remained unsolved, hate-motivation provisions are absent from that unit's criminal code, and healthcare staff routinely out patients by calling legal names. Baseline for how a unit without any procedure behaves.

A national newspaper (24 July 2024): the capital city made transfemicide a crime with sentences up to 70 years (a law approved 18 July 2024), in a setting documented as among the deadliest for trans people in the region; over 95% of homicides nationally went unpunished in 2022.
